# Undo of a popup's native close: main's superseded return projection takes the pane back from the reopened popup

## Context

`WorkstationNL.spec.mjs:2604` ("pop-out uses the Group cursor to return and replay the same live pane") is in #19657's intermittent set. It fails at the assertion "undo reopens the pane", at both screen sizes. Dev runs: [38306161797](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/actions/runs/38306161797) at 1920 and [38309244286](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/actions/runs/38309244286) at 2560.

The test pops out `commits`, returns it with a native popup close, then undoes that return. The undo restores the popup-owned document and reopens the popup, so the live pane must move into it.

Observed, on hosted probes from an unmerged branch that log every participant projection, pane resolution and window adoption after the undo:
- [Run 38324514355](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/actions/runs/38324514355): 6 of 18 runs ended with the pane visible in neither window; the test caught 4 of them. Of the other two, one passed because the assertion saw the pane in the popup just before it was taken back. The other ended unmounted in the popup's own tab container, a variant not yet explained.
- [Run 38325733035](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/actions/runs/38325733035), with a sequence id on every scheduled projection: 7 of 18 runs lost the pane. Every main refresh came from the main participant's own chain, so nothing outside it re-projected.

A lost run (all times in ms after the undo):
- At −36, the native-close return commits. Main schedules projection #4 (`commits` in main), and the popup schedules its own.
- At +4, the undo commits. Main schedules #5 (`commits` gone), and the popup schedules #5 (`commits` in the popup).
- At +235, main only now starts **#3**, from before the return. Across the lost runs that logged main, #3 starts at +107 to +241 and #4 at +854 to +1005.
- At +676, the popup projects #5 and adopts the parked pane.
- At +1005, main reaches **#4**, the return's document. At +1039 its `resolveProjectedPane('commits')` takes the live pane out of the popup's card, where it was mounted.
- Main's #5 runs about 0.8 s later and removes `commits` again. The pane ends unmounted, visible in neither window.

## The Problem

A superseded commit's projection still runs on a participant whose refresh chain is behind, and it can claim a shared live pane that a newer commit already moved elsewhere. Each participant's chain is ordered, but the two chains are not ordered against each other. Panes are single live instances resolved by identity, so whichever participant reconciles last takes the pane. That last reconcile can belong to an older snapshot.

## The Architectural Reality

- `src/manager/transaction/Commit.mjs` `complete()` dispatches each participant's projection in a microtask and refuses a superseded one: `group.snapshot !== result.snapshot` returns early. That check runs only at dispatch. At that moment the return commit is still current, so its projection is queued. It executes on the participant's chain about a second later, after the undo.
- `src/dashboard/dock/Workspace.mjs` `projectDockZoneDocument()` records `scheduledProjection = {document}` and chains the refresh on `refreshPromise`.
- `onDockProjectionFailed()` already holds the rule this case needs: a repair stands down when `scheduledProjection` has moved on, "since that newer commit's projection is the repair and the failed snapshot must not re-project over it".
- `resolveProjectedPane()` resolves a live pane by identity, wherever it is mounted.

Design authority: `Commit.complete()`'s supersession guard (a superseded snapshot does not project) and the repair path's stand-down (a superseded document must not re-project over a newer one).

## The Fix

Apply the existing supersession rule where the projection runs, not only where it is dispatched. Proposed: the chained refresh in `projectDockZoneDocument()` stands down when this participant's `scheduledProjection.document` is no longer the document it was scheduled for, as the repair path already does. A newer projection for the same participant is chained behind it and renders the current document from the live shell. A participant that a newer commit did not touch has no newer projection scheduled, so it still projects.

Alternatives, for the dock owners to weigh:
- An ownership guard in `resolveProjectedPane()`: refuse a live pane that the current Group snapshot assigns to another participant.
- Group-level ordering: project commit N+1 only after every participant has settled commit N.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] The ordering that leaves the pane outside the popup is named, with the receipt that shows it: the two runs above. Main's stale #4 resolves `commits` out of the popup after the popup has adopted it.
- [ ] A test forces that order (a participant whose chain is behind receives a superseded projection after a sibling has adopted the pane) and goes red before the fix, green after.
- [ ] `WorkstationNL.spec.mjs:2604` passes 20/20 alone on a hosted runner, with the probe's lost-pane count at 0 (post-merge receipt).

## Out of Scope

- The other popup intermittents in #19657, such as `LegacyPopupReturnNL:12`, which was a separate App-worker stall.
- Why main's chain runs a second behind. Slow refreshes are legitimate; letting a stale one claim a pane is the defect.
- The FilmTour quarantine, unless the same ordering turns out to explain it.
